behavior_in_task_description.explanation: instruction.md lists exactly four symptoms of the same UI element: (1) the attached screenshot shows the standing text clipped by the hover border, (2) temperament words 'sometimes come out in the wrong order', (3) 'a couple of neighbouring Clans' names read with "Clan" stuck on the front instead of the back', and (4) 'one relationship value doesn't get the label the game gives to every other value around it'. These map 1:1 to the four test classes in test_other_clan_box_border.py (AStandingThatTheHoverBorderCannotReach, ATemperamentThatIsReadInTheOrderTheGameRecordedIt, AClanNameThatReadsTheWayEveryOtherClanNameDoes, AStandingThatMatchesHowFriendlyTheClanActuallyIs). No filenames/coordinates are named, but that is consistent with this being a visual bug task where the screenshot is the primary spec (visual_essentiality=essential) rather than an omission of testable behavior.

behavior_in_tests.explanation: Every behavior named in instruction.md has direct f2p coverage (border clearance across long names/temperaments, temperament word order, Clan-name suffix, and the relations=7/17 boundary reading 'neutral'), and p2p tests additionally guard that already-correct behavior (short-content tiles, hover feedback, name/temperament text) is not broken by the fix. Nothing described in the instructions is left untested.

informative_test_structure.explanation: test_other_clan_box_border.py groups tests into clearly named unittest.TestCase classes, one per behavior under test (e.g. AStandingThatTheHoverBorderCannotReach, ATemperamentThatIsReadInTheOrderTheGameRecordedIt), each with a docstring explaining intent and descriptive test method names. The shared _support.py module is heavily commented, explaining the black-box observation approach (painting the UI twice, hover simulation, text-based tile discovery) so a reader can follow both what and why.

anti_cheating_measures.explanation: The Dockerfile clones the real repo, applies the three synthetic bug patches, deletes them from /tmp, strips .git before re-initializing a single-commit repo (so PR/fix history is unreachable), and never copies tests/ or solution/ into the image. The relations off-by-one and pre-existing '#text_box_22_horizcenter_spacing_95' theme id used by the fix were both verified against the real upstream repo/PR and are not fabricated giveaways. Agent-phase network is disabled (network_mode = no-network), so the agent cannot fetch the real GitHub PR/issue to read the fix.

structured_data_schema.explanation: This is a UI/visual bug-fix task operating on existing Python/pygame source files; it does not require the agent to emit structured data (JSON/CSV/API) for tests to validate.

pinned_dependencies.explanation: Runtime deps are pinned in the Dockerfile (pygame-ce==2.5.3, pygame-gui==0.6.13, ujson~=5.7, cryptography~=42.0, pgpy~=0.6, platformdirs~=3.3, requests~=2.28, strenum~=0.4, etc.), matching the project's own dependency constraints. The test-only dependency pytest is pinned separately in test.sh (pytest~=8.2) rather than baked into the image.

typos.explanation: No typos found in instruction.md, task.toml, or the test/verifier scripts. 'eeever so slightly' in the task title looks unusual but was confirmed to be a verbatim copy of the real upstream GitHub issue title (#4978), not an authoring typo.

tests_or_solution_in_image.explanation: The Dockerfile only COPYs assets/ (screenshot) into the image after removing assets/bugs/; it explicitly states 'tests/ and solution/ are intentionally NOT copied into the image' and they are supplied at verify time via bind mounts, per test.sh applying /tests/test.patch and solve.sh applying /solution/fix.patch from outside the image.

test_deps_in_image.explanation: pytest is deliberately excluded from the Dockerfile's pip install list (with a comment confirming this) and is instead installed inside tests/test.sh at verify time, keeping the agent-facing image free of test-only tooling.

hardcoded_solution.explanation: solve.sh applies solution/fix.patch via git apply/patch, which makes the actual multi-hunk source-code edits (label rect repositioning, text template swap, temperament index swap, relations comparison operator, theme object id change) rather than printing or echoing a final answer. This was cross-checked against the real upstream fix commit (1edd03aa0) and matches it for the genuine bug plus the two additional synthetic-defect reversions.

file_reference_mentioned.explanation: The task does not require the agent to produce new output files; the fix is made directly to existing source files (scripts/screens/LeaderDenScreen.py, scripts/clan.py), which are the same files listed in task.toml's files_edited, and tests exercise the running UI code rather than checking for generated artifacts.
